known.title: Not done: `forge lanes --aws setup` refuses a public repo
Functional: AWS setup rejects documented self-hosted Linux runners
Gate: the new AWS controls are absent from the Forge guide
Test: default workflow compatibility and AWS test-group routing
Follow-up: accept the AWS European Sovereign Cloud region

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security
Case: normal use - A developer works on a public github.com checkout while `GH_HOST` points to an authenticated GitHub Enterprise host containing a private repo with the same owner and name. The repair removes `GH_REPO`, but `_origin_repo` discards the origin hostname at `src/forge/aws.py:76`, and this call supplies no `--hostname`. [GitHub CLI selects its default host](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/pkg/cmd/api/api.go), so it reads the Enterprise repo. The `full_name` comparison then passes, and setup accepts the public checkout instead of refusing it.
findings.title: Not done: `forge lanes --aws setup` refuses a public repo

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A repo upgrades with AWS runners off or configures two pull-request test groups on AWS. The proof still has no pre-change workflow baseline: its byte comparison at line 111 compares two outputs from the same renderer, so a changed default workflow can pass. Also, this two-group assertion is satisfied by the nightly `full-suite` matrix; the pull-request matrix uses a different expression at `src/forge/prcheck.py:93`. The test would still pass if the AWS pull-request workflow ran only one group.
findings.title: Test: default workflow compatibility and AWS test-group routing
